channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Vape Tax Needs Watching
item.description: Vape tax needs watching because small price changes can become big behaviour changes. For adults who have switched from smoking, affordability can help keep the lower-risk option within reach; for those still smoking, it can influence whether switching feels realistic at all. A poorly calibrated tax may push people back towards cigarettes or towards cheaper illicit products. The test should be simple: does the policy keep movement away from combustion attractive, or does it make that progress harder to sustain? (Published on October 13, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: Eight EU Capitals Want to Ban Products That Don’t Exist Yet
item.description: Banning products before they even exist is not precaution; it is policy closing its eyes to innovation. Eight EU capitals pushing restrictions on future nicotine products risk freezing the market around what already exists, including cigarettes. New products should face evidence, standards and scrutiny, not pre-emptive exclusion based on category fear. A smarter European approach would regulate risk as it emerges, while keeping the door open to technologies that could help move smokers further away from combustion. (Published on October 13, 2026byweareinnovation.global)

item.title: UK smoking falls below one in 10 ahead of nicotine pouch age restrictions
item.description: The UK’s smoking rate falling below one in ten is a milestone worth protecting. It has happened alongside wider use of smoke-free nicotine products, which makes upcoming pouch restrictions especially important to get right. Age limits can help prevent youth access, but they should not blur the role pouches may play for adults looking for alternatives to cigarettes. The next phase of UK policy should keep the focus on the outcome that matters most: fewer people smoking. (Published on October 13, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Media Watch: The WSJ Suggests Wellness Types Are Rehabilitating Nicotine
item.description: Nicotine entering wellness culture creates a communication challenge public health cannot ignore. A product may be smoke-free and far less harmful than cigarettes, but that does not make nicotine a lifestyle supplement or a harmless productivity tool. The clearest message is also the most nuanced: non-combustible nicotine can matter for smokers moving away from combustion, while non-users should not be encouraged to start. Risk communication needs to hold both truths at once. (Published on October 13, 2026bydaily-pouch.com)

item.title: Brussels is funding the voices that tell it what it wants to hear
item.description: Brussels’ nicotine debate has a transparency problem when public money funds organisations that then echo the Commission’s preferred line. The article points to a “market freeze” backed by several health ministers that would restrict future nicotine products while cigarettes remain available. That should concern anyone interested in evidence-based regulation. Public health policy needs independent scrutiny, consumer voices and open funding trails — especially when decisions could limit lower-risk alternatives for millions of adults who smoke. (Published on October 13, 2026bybrusselstimes.com)
